questions.question: A startup wants to run event-driven image-resizing code with zero server management and pay only per execution. Which service model fits best?
questions.explanation: FaaS runs event-triggered functions with no provisioning and bills only for execution time. It is ideal for short, bursty tasks like image processing.

questions.question: A company must run legacy software that requires full control of the OS kernel and custom drivers in the cloud. Which service model should it choose?
questions.explanation: Only IaaS gives customers control of the guest OS, kernel, and drivers. PaaS and SaaS abstract away that layer entirely.

questions.question: A hospital must keep patient records on-premises for compliance but wants to use public cloud analytics on anonymized data. Which deployment model fits?
questions.explanation: Hybrid cloud keeps regulated data in private infrastructure while bursting or offloading other workloads to public cloud, balancing compliance with flexibility.

questions.question: A firm runs production workloads on both AWS and Google Cloud specifically to avoid dependence on a single vendor. What strategy is this?
questions.explanation: Multi-cloud spreads workloads across multiple public providers, reducing vendor lock-in and improving resilience if one provider has an outage.

questions.question: An e-commerce site experiences sudden, unpredictable traffic spikes during flash sales. Which cloud capability should it rely on to handle these spikes cost-effectively?
questions.explanation: Elasticity automatically adds instances during the spike and releases them afterward, so the site pays only for capacity actually needed instead of permanent overprovisioning.

questions.question: A research team runs overnight batch jobs that can be restarted if interrupted and wants the lowest possible compute cost. Which instance type should it use?
questions.explanation: Spot instances offer discounts up to 90 percent but can be reclaimed anytime. Fault-tolerant, restartable batch work is the classic use case.

questions.question: An application will run at steady, predictable load 24/7 for the next three years. Which pricing model minimizes its cost?
questions.explanation: Committing to a multi-year term unlocks the deepest discounts for predictable workloads. On-demand would cost far more over three years; spot is too risky for steady production.

questions.question: To survive a complete data-center outage without downtime, an application should be deployed across multiple what within a region?
questions.explanation: Availability zones are isolated facilities with independent power and networking. Multi-AZ deployment keeps the app running if one facility fails.

questions.question: A global streaming service needs to deliver video with low latency to users worldwide. Which cloud service should cache content near users?
questions.explanation: CDNs cache content at edge locations close to end users, cutting latency and offloading origin servers. CloudFront and Cloudflare are common examples.

questions.question: A company performs a lift-and-shift migration, moving its existing VMs to the cloud unchanged. Which service model is it using?
questions.explanation: Lift-and-shift rehosts existing VMs on cloud infrastructure without redesigning the application, which is the IaaS model.

questions.question: Developers push code to a repository and the platform automatically builds and runs it without any server setup. Which model are they using?
questions.explanation: PaaS abstracts the entire runtime stack: developers supply code, and the platform handles build, deployment, scaling, and infrastructure.

questions.question: In Kubernetes, what is the smallest deployable unit that groups one or more containers sharing storage and network resources?
questions.explanation: A pod is the atomic scheduling unit in Kubernetes. Containers in a pod share a network namespace and storage volumes and are always co-located on the same node.

questions.question: A piece of code runs for 100 milliseconds per request and is billed per invocation plus execution duration. Which execution model is this?
questions.explanation: Per-invocation, per-millisecond billing with no idle cost is the defining trait of FaaS platforms like AWS Lambda.

questions.question: Regulations require a company's data to physically remain within its country's borders. Which cloud construct should it select when provisioning resources?
questions.explanation: Choosing the correct region keeps data resident in a specific geography for data-sovereignty compliance. Providers also offer sovereign or government regions for stricter rules.

questions.question: An engineer provisions a new server through a web portal at midnight with no call to the provider. Which NIST cloud characteristic does this demonstrate?
questions.explanation: On-demand self-service lets consumers provision resources unilaterally at any time. It is one of the five essential NIST cloud characteristics.

questions.question: A company runs three on-demand VMs billed at $0.10 per hour each, 24 hours a day for an entire 30-day month. What is the total compute bill for those VMs?
questions.explanation: 3 VMs x $0.10/hr x 24 hr/day x 30 days = $216. On-demand billing multiplies hourly price by running hours.

questions.question: A provider advertises a 99.9% monthly uptime SLA. Roughly how much downtime per month does this SLA permit?
questions.explanation: A 30-day month is 43,200 minutes; 0.1% of that is about 43.2 minutes of allowed downtime.

questions.question: A distributed cloud database suffers a network partition between two regions. According to the CAP theorem, between which two properties must designers choose?
questions.explanation: CAP states a partitioned system can guarantee at most one of consistency or availability; partition tolerance must be kept.

questions.question: An organization keeps only its databases replicated and core components minimally running in a second region, spinning up full capacity only during disaster recovery. What DR pattern is this?
questions.explanation: Pilot light keeps only essential core systems (like replicated data) always on; servers are provisioned only at failover, cheaper than warm standby.

questions.question: An application stores billions of photos addressed by unique keys with metadata in a flat namespace, like Amazon S3. What storage type is it using?
questions.explanation: Object storage manages data as objects with metadata and unique IDs in a flat namespace, unlike hierarchical file or raw block storage.
